macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Fed holds rates steady; December hike expectations rise
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 decision, while two officials dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Markets increased the implied probability of a December hike to 87.4%, from 78.3% the previous day.

items.title: U.S. stocks finish nearly flat after Fed decision
items.summary: The Dow rose 0.17% to 52,469.11 and the S&P 500 gained 0.08% to 7,728.60, while the Nasdaq fell 0.16% to 26,434.50. Investors awaited earnings from Microsoft and Alphabet for further signals on artificial-intelligence spending and technology valuations.

items.title: Oil prices jump on Middle East supply concerns
items.summary: Crude prices climbed after Iran-backed Houthis attacked a refinery in Saudi Arabia, raising concerns about potential disruption to regional energy supplies.

items.title: Vertiv raises outlook as data-center demand supports results
items.summary: Vertiv surged 16.8% after beating quarterly expectations and increasing its full-year revenue and profit forecasts, reflecting strong demand for digital infrastructure linked to artificial-intelligence buildouts.

items.title: SK Hynix reports sharp profit surge; chip stocks gain
items.summary: SK Hynix reported a record quarterly operating profit that was nearly seven times higher than a year earlier and exceeded market expectations. Micron rose 4.7% in U.S. trading as investors reassessed demand for memory chips and AI infrastructure.

items.title: Robinhood profit misses expectations
items.summary: Robinhood fell 3.9% after weaker cryptocurrency activity contributed to third-quarter profit below analyst forecasts.

items.title: Boston Scientific cuts annual profit forecast
items.summary: Boston Scientific dropped 2.9% after trimming its full-year profit outlook, making it one of the notable earnings-related decliners in the session.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $80,000 as traders await Fed decision
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $80,500–$81,000 after briefly falling below $80,000, while ether gained roughly 1.4%. A reported 14,942 BTC left exchanges in one day, the largest outflow in five weeks, according to cited Santiment data.

items.title: Binance seeks Brazilian license and delists 22 tokens
items.summary: Binance applied for authorization from Brazil’s central bank ahead of the October 30 deadline. It also restricted eight services and delisted 22 tokens for Brazilian users to comply with new regulations.

items.title: Ripple receives final approval for U.S. national trust bank
items.summary: Ripple received final approval from a U.S. banking regulator for Ripple National Trust Bank. The institution is expected to custody assets supporting the RLUSD stablecoin and hold crypto for businesses, but it cannot accept deposits or make loans.

items.title: South Korea may delay cryptocurrency gains tax until 2029
items.summary: South Korea’s presidential office is reportedly considering postponing the planned 22% cryptocurrency gains tax, scheduled to begin in January 2027, until 2029.

items.title: Aviva Investors launches tokenized fund shares on XRP Ledger
items.summary: Aviva Investors and Ripple made a tokenized share class of the Aviva Investors Sterling Liquidity Fund available on the XRP Ledger, with Aviva investing £50 million. The underlying fund remains off-chain.

items.title: Liquid Network redemption freeze continues after bitcoin exploit
items.summary: Liquid Network has kept LBTC-to-bitcoin redemptions paused for 35 days after an attacker exploited an Elements software vulnerability. The attacker reportedly still controls about 598.5 BTC, valued at roughly $49.7 million.

items.title: Mantle proposes lower annual core budget
items.summary: Mantle released MIP-35, proposing to cap its core budget for July 2026 through June 2027 at $40 million in USDx and 150 million MNT, down from $52 million and 200 million MNT in the previous cycle.

items.title: Itaú launches cryptocurrency trading and custody in Brazil
items.summary: Brazilian bank Itaú Unibanco began offering cryptocurrency trading and custody under the central bank’s new regulatory framework, initially supporting 15 crypto assets including BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and USDC.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA reportedly closes BioWare after 30 years
items.summary: Electronic Arts reportedly shut down BioWare, ending the studio’s three-decade run and halting early development on the next Mass Effect project. The report has not been independently confirmed by a primary EA or BioWare announcement.

items.title: Warhorse Studios confirms cyberattack
items.summary: Warhorse Studios, developer of Kingdom Come: Deliverance, confirmed that attackers gained unauthorized access to its systems and said it is investigating the incident and potential data exposure.

items.title: GTA VI sets record purchase interest in Circana tracking
items.summary: Nearly 29% of U.S. console and PC gamers reportedly plan to buy Grand Theft Auto VI, the highest purchase-intent figure recorded by Circana for a video game. Rockstar is scheduled to release the game on November 19.

items.title: Nintendo announces Indie World Showcase
items.summary: Nintendo announced an Indie World presentation for October 28, expected to feature new and upcoming independent games for its platforms.

items.title: Probably Stolen launches on Steam
items.summary: The cyberpunk simulation game Probably Stolen was released on Steam and reportedly set a new player-record milestone for publisher tinyBuild.

items.title: PlayStation reveals Prism transparent-accessory collection
items.summary: PlayStation presented a Prism collection featuring transparent DualSense controllers and matching PS5 console covers.

items.title: KartBoard Dash announces competitive mode and console versions
items.summary: Following its PC and mobile launch, KartBoard Dash developer Zatun announced a Championship Mode and plans to bring the free-to-play racer to PlayStation 5, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch.

items.title: PlayStation reveals Where Winds Meet story expansion
items.summary: PlayStation detailed the climactic Hutuo Battlefield narrative arc for Where Winds Meet, scheduled to launch on November 13.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple unveils touchscreen MacBook Pro and updated iMac
items.summary: Apple announced new Mac and iMac hardware featuring its latest processors, including a touchscreen MacBook Pro with a 14-inch or 16-inch display. The MacBook Pro starts at $2,899, according to Techmeme’s roundup.

items.title: Amazon announces new Echo devices and Alexa features
items.summary: Amazon introduced the $500 Echo Show 16, the $200 Echo Time alarm clock and a new Alexa Photo Frame, while also raising prices for some smart speakers. The company also previewed Alexa Home Map.

items.title: FCC approves Amazon Leo acquisition of Globalstar
items.summary: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission approved Amazon Leo’s $11.5 billion acquisition of Globalstar, giving Amazon access to Globalstar’s satellite fleet and mobile-satellite spectrum.

items.title: Dropbox plans approximately 200 layoffs
items.summary: Dropbox said it plans to cut about 6% of its workforce, or roughly 200 jobs, with expected severance costs of $27 million to $33 million. CTO Ali Dasdan is also scheduled to leave on November 18.

items.title: Anduril and Qualcomm announce rugged BlueChip laptop
items.summary: Anduril and Qualcomm unveiled BlueChip, a rugged laptop aimed at government and defense customers. Preorders are expected to open in 2027, with most first-generation components sourced from the United States or allied countries.
